notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP fetch of homepage, robots.txt, sitemap index, and the India-specific category sitemap https://www.ikea.com/sitemaps/cat-en-IN_1.xml which lists all ~1022 India category/PLP URLs) was used for full-taxonomy discovery. robots.txt (fetched from ikea.com root; www.ikea.com/in/en/robots.txt itself 404s) has no Claude-specific disallow and only blocks generic crawl-trap params (search, filters, sort) -- not category browsing, so Tier 1 was permitted. Tier 3 (Claude-in-Chrome, since no separate Playwright tool was available) was used selectively to verify true item counts on categories whose JSON-LD numberOfItems equalled/approached the 24-item first-page cap, because rendered page text ("Showing 24 of 119 results", "Show more") proved the JSON-LD figure is only the first batch, not the true total, on paginated categories. Verified via browser: Rakhi gifting (JSON-LD said 24, actual page said 'Showing 24 of 119 results' -> true qty 119), Swedish Easter (JSON-LD 24 -> true 31), Swedish Midsummer (JSON-LD 24 -> true 47), and one control case Holiday cooking & baking (JSON-LD 21 -> page confirmed 'Showing 21 of 21 results', i.e. any JSON-LD count already below 24 is the true, complete count with no further pagination). All other qty values below 24 were therefore taken directly from JSON-LD ItemList numberOfItems without further browser verification, consistent with the confirmed pattern. A nonsense slug (cat/zzznonsenseXYZ123-99999/) and several guessed Diwali slugs (diwali, diwali-decor, diwali-decoration, diwali-collection, diwali-49149, etc.) all 301-redirected identically to a generic fallback category (home-decor-de001), confirming guessed URLs are not real taxonomy and that no Diwali category exists via URL guessing. INCLUDED: two real IKEA hub structures found via the India category sitemap -- (1) the 'Christmas Collections' hub (christmas-collections-wt001) with its 14 genuine PLP sub-categories (Christmas decoration, lights, flower pots & plants, flower pots & vases, table decoration, tableware, textiles, tree ornaments & accessories, trees & plants, stationery/wrapping/gift bags, the VINTERFINT collection, plus 'Holiday cooking & baking', 'Holiday foods', 'Holiday dinner' which share the same 49xxx ID block and appear in the same hub's breadcrumb ('Products > Christmas Collections > ...') despite being labelled 'Holiday' rather than 'Christmas' -- confirmed as the same Christmas taxonomy cluster, not a separate occasion); and (2) the 'Seasonal celebrations' hub (seasonal-celebrations-700321) with 5 genuine dated-holiday PLPs: Swedish Christmas dinner, Swedish Easter, Swedish Midsummer, Swedish Crayfish party (Kräftskiva -- a genuine recurring Swedish calendar festival, treated identically in the site's own taxonomy to Halloween/Christmas/Easter under the same hub), and Halloween dinner party. Separately, a standalone India-specific festival category was found and verified: 'Rakhi gifting made meaningful' (rakhi-gifting-700834, breadcrumb 'Shops > Rakhi gifting made meaningful', body copy 'Celebrating the sibling bond ... this Rakshabandhan'), a genuine PLP with sort/filter and a real product grid -- mapped to Raksha Bandhan. EXCLUDED after inspection: 'Deals on Christmas Trees, Lights & Decor | Festive Sale' (offers/deals-on-...-wt001) -- a storewide sale/clearance page, not a genuine category, per boundary rules. 'Holiday Gifting' (holiday-gifting-49233) -- 0 numberOfItems, 0 product links, pure marketing copy ('Discover a range of thoughtful gifts... bringing joy and warmth to the season') with no actual product grid -- a gift-guide/editorial landing page, fails the genuine-PLP test. 'Celebrations' (celebrations-700794) -- a generic cross-category hub filtered by product type (kitchen/textile/decor) rather than tied to one specific holiday; no specific festival name or copy, fails the specific-holiday test. 'The Autumn shop' (autumn-700796) and its linked 'Höstagille collection' (hoestagille-collection-700570) -- a general seasonal (fall) merchandising theme, not a specific holiday/festival, excluded per the same logic that would exclude a generic 'Spring collection'. CHECKED AND CONFIRMED ABSENT (searched full India category sitemap of 1022 URLs plus homepage HTML) with zero matches for: Diwali, Holi, Navratri, Dussehra, Ganesh(-Chaturthi), Pongal, Onam, Eid, Ramzan/Ramadan, Valentine, Mother's Day, Father's Day, Thanksgiving, New Year/New-Year. This is a genuine, thoroughly-checked absence (not a search false-negative) -- unlike IKEA UAE/Japan, IKEA India's own taxonomy carries no dedicated Diwali, Holi, or other major Indian-festival PLP despite India being IKEA's storefront market; the only India-specific festival category found is Raksha Bandhan (Rakhi gifting). The Christmas-collections hub and Seasonal-celebrations hub are recorded as is_group grouping rows (their children are subsets, not double-counted).
